text: Roughly once a year, Venus returns to the exact place it occupied when you were born, and for a few days to a week or two your capacity for pleasure gets refreshed at the source. It is the one visit in her circuit that lands on your own taste directly, with no other planet translating. The conjunction fuses the Venus in the sky with the Venus in you: what you love, what you find beautiful, what you need from other people in order to feel warm. While it lasts, those needs stop being background. You want company, or comfort, or color, and the wanting is specific. Old pleasures taste good again. People respond to you more readily, because you are more openly yourself in the ways that draw others in. The period favors everything Venus governs: affection, friendship, beauty, and money in its small enjoyable forms. It is a natural time to freshen how you look, to fill the house with something lovely, to say the fond thing out loud, or simply to enjoy what you already have with more attention than usual. Nothing here forces. The risk is only mild indulgence, a little extra spending or sweetness beyond what the week needed. The arc is short but real. As the conjunction applies, your mood softens and your appetite for pleasure wakes up, sometimes with a restless edge, as if something pleasant is due. The exact pass is the sweet spot, often a day or two when affection flows easily in both directions and your taste feels sure. As Venus separates, the glow settles into ordinary liking, and whatever you enjoyed most tends to stay in the rotation. In some years Venus is slowing toward its occasional retrograde near this point, and the visit then comes in two or three passes over a longer stretch; when that happens, the repeated visits usually mean a deeper review of what you love rather than more parties. Most years, one clean pass is the whole story. Because the visit recurs annually, it makes a quiet yearly checkpoint. What delighted you last time may leave you flat now, and something you never used to notice may suddenly please you. That drift matters. Taste is one of the most honest records of who you are becoming, and this transit lets you read it once a year without effort. Treat the period as a small season of liking what you like, openly, and it does its work: your affections come out of it restocked, and the year of Venus weather that follows starts from a warmer place.

What you like and what is available briefly agree. For a few days, twice in most years, transiting Venus holds a sextile to your natal Venus, and the world's current offerings happen to fit your standing tastes: the gathering is the kind you actually enjoy, the person free for lunch is one you genuinely miss, the thing on sale is the thing you would have chosen at full price. The period runs on low resistance rather than luck. Your affections do not change during it; acting on them just gets cheaper. The friend you always mean to see, the corner of the house you always mean to improve, the standing pleasure you keep deferring on the grounds that any week would do, all of these come within easy reach while the angle holds, and they are its proper use. This is a transit for the loves you already have. Company flows without management, and you are somewhat better company yourself, more patient with the small frictions of other people's ways, quicker to be pleased. That slight rise in agreeableness is often the whole visible evidence of the transit. Where taste is concerned, the days favor the confirmed preference over the experiment: the reliable restaurant, the medium you already work in, the color you always come back to. Choices made in this weather feel like recognition rather than discovery, and they wear well. The mechanics barely register. Venus applies over a day or two, holds the angle exactly for about a day, and the ease is gone within the week, having demanded nothing and predicted nothing. Miss it and the calendar simply moves on; another pass comes within months, and in a rare retrograde year the same contact can repeat over a longer stretch, giving a neglected pleasure two or three separate hearings. The stakes stay small on purpose. But small is different from trivial, and the arithmetic of these passes deserves respect. A life ends up furnished, in people and in things, largely by whether easy affection got acted on while acting was easy, and this transit is precisely that opening, twice a year, on schedule. Take the lunch. Hang the picture. Send the fond, slightly unnecessary message. None of it will look like an event, and none of it needs to. The reward for treating your own likings as worth an afternoon is a daily life that quietly matches you, and daily life is where Venus, whatever the aspect, finally lives or does not.

Comfort stops fitting quite right for a few days. Transiting Venus is square your natal Venus, and the two pull in different directions: the pleasures on offer around you sit at odds with the pleasures you actually run on. The classic signature is a restless dissatisfaction that is hard to justify. The people you love are the same people, the room is the same room, and yet you feel underfed, a little unappreciated, inclined to sulk or to soothe yourself with treats. Spending often rises during this transit, not from need but from mood, since buying something pretty is the fastest imitation of being cared for. In relationships the square shows up as friction over small wants: how to spend the evening, whose taste prevails, who has been doing more of the affection lately. None of it is large, but a square forces what a softer aspect would let slide, and the forcing is useful. Wanting is information. The discontent of these days points straight at needs you have been meeting on autopilot or not meeting at all. While the square is applying, the itch builds and you may not name it as Venus at all, just an irritability around pleasure, a sense that nothing sounds good. Near the exact pass the friction tends to surface in one concrete form: a minor clash with someone close, a purchase you second-guess, an invitation that annoys you by existing. As Venus separates, the static clears quickly, and what remains is a slightly sharper picture of what you want. This square comes around roughly twice a year in Venus's annual circuit and lasts days rather than weeks, so it never asks for endurance, only honesty. In some years a retrograde brings Venus back over the same angle another time or two, stretching the mood into a longer review of your tastes and attachments; that is the exception, not the rule. The workable response is modest. Say the small want out loud instead of resenting its absence. Let a difference in taste be a difference, not a verdict on the relationship. Put a day between the urge to buy and the buying, since the urge often expires overnight. Handled that way, the transit functions like a tuning check on your affections. You come out of it knowing a little more precisely what comfort means to you now, which is exactly the knowledge the easier Venus days will spend.

Twice around the year, Venus in the sky settles into a trine with the Venus you were born with, and for up to a week or so the social weather clears. Nothing in it confronts you; the trine simply lets your affections run at their natural angle. Company feels easy, including your own. Conversations soften. People who are usually prickly with you are less so, and you are less so with them, since the aspect works on your side of the exchange first. Your sense of beauty is reliable now: things you choose during a Venus trine, from what you wear to how a room comes together, tend to still please you later, which is not true of every mood. The tradition marks these days as favorable for anything that runs on goodwill: gatherings, reconciliations, first dates, asking a favor, showing work that needs a kind audience. Pleasure arrives without much cost, and affection given now is usually returned in kind. The one caution trines always carry applies here too. Ease invites drift. It is possible to spend the whole pass pleasantly on the couch and let its goodwill go unused, and because the transit recurs about twice a year, missing one is never a disaster, just a small waste. There is nothing abrupt anywhere in the pass. The trine announces itself as a lightening of tone you might credit to sleep or weather. Venus's warmest stretch is the day or two she holds the angle exactly, when relations flow most freely and your charm needs no management, and the ease tapers so gradually afterward that you rarely notice it end. In some years, Venus retrograding nearby can bring this trine back twice more over a longer window, turning a pleasant few days into a pleasant season with a review in the middle; most years it is a single clean pass. What grows in you through these small regular visits is not dramatic. It is the practiced knowledge of what your affections feel like when nothing is wrong: a baseline of warmth you can recognize and steer back toward in harder weather. Use one of these passes to mend something slightly bent, or just to enjoy the people you have on purpose, and the transit has done everything a few easy days can do.

Once a year, Venus stands directly across the sky from the place it holds in your chart, and for some days your wants meet everyone else's face to face. An opposition confronts, and this one confronts gently but clearly: what pleases you is put across the table from what pleases the people around you, and the difference becomes visible. A partner's taste, a friend's idea of a good weekend, a colleague's notion of fair, each lands with a little more contrast than usual. The transit is not harsh, but it is revealing. Under softer sky you and yours blur your preferences together for the sake of peace; under this one, the seams show. Affection itself often runs high during the pass. Oppositions with Venus tend to pull other people close rather than push them away, and the classic events are social: an invitation you feel obliged to weigh, a relationship conversation that has been waiting, generosity from someone that carries a quiet expectation. The question underneath the days is balance. Who accommodates whom, and does the ledger of small kindnesses feel fair to both sides? While the opposition applies, you may notice a rising wish to be met halfway, or a vague sense of being over-adapted to someone else's comfort. At the exact pass the contrast peaks, sometimes as a mild standoff over plans or money, more often as a plain sighting of how differently two people relax. As Venus separates, most of the tension resolves into adjustment, one small renegotiation of the shared evening, the shared budget, the shared silence. Venus oppositions run days, occasionally toward two weeks, and return every year, so no single pass carries much weight on its own. In some years a retrograde folds the opposition into a longer back-and-forth with two or three contacts, and then the balancing act becomes a real theme for a while rather than an afternoon's weather. The growth available here is relational rather than private. Your own taste you can study any time; what this transit teaches is how your wants behave in company, where you concede too fast, where you dig in over trivia, where the trade is genuinely even. Read one pass a year with that question in mind and your closest ties get slightly truer each time, which is the kind of compound interest Venus likes best.

For a few days to a couple of weeks, Venus crosses the degree your natal Mars holds, and warmth fuses with drive. These are two planets that want each other's company: Venus carries attraction, pleasure, and the wish to connect, Mars carries desire, initiative, and heat. Conjoined, they run as one current, and you feel it as magnetism. Wanting becomes less complicated. If you are drawn to someone, the pull is frank; if you are making something, the making has appetite in it; if you are in a settled relationship, the settled part warms up. The transit has an honest physical streak. Romance under it tends to skip preliminaries, and creative work done now often has more body than polish, which is usually a fair trade. Charm and assertion cooperate instead of taking turns, so this is a natural window for the direct approach: expressing interest, opening a delicate negotiation, asking plainly for what you want in love or in money. People read your directness as warmth rather than pressure while the blend holds. The applying days bring a build of restless, pleasant energy, a sense of being more visible and more interested in being visible. The exact pass is the peak of the charge, and its events are usually small but vivid: a spark with someone, a burst of productive making, an evening with more color than the calendar promised. As Venus separates, the heat banks down into ordinary affection and ordinary effort, and whatever you started keeps whatever momentum you gave it. The pass recurs roughly once a year, and in some years a Venus retrograde walks it back across your Mars for a second and third touch, stretching a spark into a slower burn with a reconsidering phase in the middle. That is occasional, not typical. The main caution is impulsiveness of the enjoyable kind. Desire this fluent can spend money, make promises, or start entanglements at a pace the following month has to finance. Nothing in the transit is reckless by itself; it simply removes the usual pause between wanting and reaching. Keep a thin margin of judgment around the biggest reaches and let the rest run. What the period builds, used well, is confidence in your own directness: proof that you can want something openly, act on it warmly, and have that received as attractive rather than too much. That lesson outlasts the transit by a long way.

Venus at a sextile to your natal Mars opens a short, friendly channel between what you want and how you go after it. The offer, and a sextile is always an offer, is coordination: for a few days your charm and your drive work the same shift. Approaches you would normally overthink come out naturally. You can be direct without an edge and warm without going soft, which is a rarer combination than it sounds. Socially, the period favors first moves of every size, from starting a conversation with a stranger to reviving a flirtation to proposing the plan your group has been circling for weeks. In work and creative life, the aspect lends appetite to projects that need both taste and push, the kind where you must make something and also make it appealing. Cooperative efforts go well now because you instinctively sweeten your asks; people find it easy to say yes to you and hard to say why. None of this happens by itself. The sextile improves conditions, not outcomes, and its few days pass politely if you spend them waiting. Venus is in and out of this angle within days. On her way in you may just feel sociable and slightly bolder, with energy that wants somewhere pleasant to go, and her day or two at exact favors the move itself, the ask, the invitation, the pitch, the date. On her way out the boldness cools first and the warmth lingers a little longer, so late in the pass you consolidate rather than initiate. Expect the angle roughly twice a year as Venus makes its annual circuit, each visit brief; in some years a retrograde grants a repeat or two, and an overture that fell flat gets an unforced second chance. Treat that as a bonus, never a plan. There is also a quieter use of these days that the tradition notes: they are good for putting warmth into effort you already owe. Chores shared with someone, work done for people you like, exercise taken as pleasure rather than discipline, all go better under this sky. What you learn from a well-used pass is the feel of desire and grace pulling together, and once you have felt it, you can sometimes recreate the blend on ordinary days. That is the sextile's long game: it shows you a cooperation you can practice.

Attraction picks up an edge for a few days. Venus square your natal Mars sets the planet of affection at a hard angle to your planet of desire and drive, and the two stop cooperating: you want closeness and you want your own way, at the same time, from the same people. The friction is rarely large, but a square forces it into the open. Classic forms include bickering with a partner over nothing either of you can name afterward, irritation at someone precisely because you find them attractive, flirtation with a competitive undertone, and the special impatience of wanting to be pleased right now by people who did not get the memo. Appetite in general runs hot and slightly contrary. Purchases lean impulsive, indulgence leans excessive, and charm can come out with too much push behind it, reading as pressure where you meant play. Underneath the static, the square is doing legitimate work. It surfaces the standing tension every person carries between tenderness and assertion, and it shows you your current settings. If the pass makes you snappish, some want has gone unspoken too long. If it makes you passive and resentful, you have been buying peace at your own expense. Either finding is worth having. The applying days build a vague friction, energy without a satisfying outlet, sweetness that keeps missing its timing. Near the exact pass the spark usually grounds itself somewhere specific: one quarrel, one charged encounter, one purchase or promise made at a heat the cooler week must honor. Separating, the irritation drains fast, often leaving a better conversation than the calm days ever produced, since squares at least get things said. The angle returns about twice a year for a few days each time, and in some years a Venus retrograde drags it back across the same degrees once or twice more, turning a spat into a season's recurring theme until its real subject gets addressed. The useful discipline is small: pause between impulse and action, especially with money and with words that cannot be unsaid, and name the want under the mood while the mood is still warm. Couples who treat these days as weather rather than verdict often find the friction converts directly into heat of the better kind. What you keep afterward is a slightly more honest account of your desires, which makes every easier Venus transit that follows work better.

There are transits that hand you energy and transits that hand you ease; Venus trine your natal Mars hands you both at once, blended. For up to a week or so, desire and affection run in the same direction without friction, and the effect is a kind of relaxed vitality. You act on what you want without rehearsing it, and the acting has grace. Where the conjunction of these two runs hot and the square runs contrary, the trine simply aligns them, so the days feel less like an event and more like yourself on a good week. The alignment shows everywhere the two planets reach. In love, warmth and initiative take turns smoothly: you pursue without pushing and receive without going passive, and existing relationships often get a spontaneous lift, an evening that turns out better than planned. Socially you carry more magnetism than usual and, more useful, better timing about when to use it. Physical life benefits too; movement, effort, and pleasure sit close together now, and work done with the hands or the body carries satisfaction beyond its result. Creative projects favor these days especially, since taste and force, the critic and the maker, stop arguing. Little of this is loud. Your mood warms and small frictions stop catching as Venus moves into range; the best flow comes while she holds the trine, when approaches land and efforts feel frictionless; and the week simply keeps going well for a while after she has moved on, so you often credit the transit only in hindsight. The trine comes around roughly twice a year, briefly, and in some years a retrograde grants it a return engagement or two across a longer span. Its only real hazard is the trine's usual one: ease used as a reason to do nothing. A flow state wasted on scrolling is still wasted. The remedy is to aim the current at something, anything you want, since wanting is exactly what is well-tuned right now: the conversation you have been saving, the project that needs a fearless hour, the person who deserves a warm and direct word. Used that way, the pass leaves a residue worth having, evidence of how you operate when desire and kindness agree. That memory becomes a standard you can steer by, and steering by it is how a few easy days improve the ordinary ones.

When Venus moves into opposition with your natal Mars, attraction and friction arrive in the same package, usually carried by another person. The opposition puts the transit's theme across the table: your Mars, the part of you that asserts, pursues, and defends, is faced by the sky's current voice for charm, pleasure, and relation. In practice the days often feature someone whose warmth provokes you or whose provocation is oddly warm. Old couples know this weather; it is the stretch where affection and irritation take turns so quickly they seem to be one feeling. Newer connections formed or heated under it tend to run polarized, strong pull, strong sparks, and the pull is real even when the sparks are noise. The confrontation underneath is about the trade between pleasing and prevailing. During the pass you can feel pulled to accommodate until you resent it, or to push until you charm no one, and the people opposite you are running the same seesaw from the other end. Negotiation is the aspect's native mode. Deals, plans, and standing arrangements with partners come up for adjustment now, and the adjustments hold better when both appetites get named instead of one side quietly folding. Sensitivity climbs as Venus draws into place opposite your Mars: compliments and slights both land harder, and you notice exactly who is meeting you halfway. The scene, when it comes, tends to arrive with her at full opposition, a charged conversation, a flare of jealousy or desire, a standoff over something small standing in for something real. Once she begins to move off, the heat drops and the actual settlement gets made, often more easily than the drama suggested. The pass runs days, occasionally stretching toward two weeks, and returns roughly yearly; in some years Venus's occasional retrograde replays it once or twice, giving a charged relationship question a second and third round before it settles. What the opposition offers, past the drama, is calibration. You find out where your line between warmth and self-assertion actually sits by watching someone stand on it. Handled with any honesty, the days convert into franker affection: heat acknowledged, terms adjusted, resentment spent before it aged. The connections that matter often come out of this transit closer than they went in, not because it was gentle, but because it made both sides show their hand.

A few days arrive each year when transiting Venus crosses your natal Jupiter, joining the sky's two traditional benefics at one degree, and the tone of life sweetens noticeably. The conjunction fuses Venus's affection and taste with Jupiter's generosity and reach, and the mixture is one of the most pleasant short transits there is. Warmth scales up. You feel expansive toward people and they return it with interest; hospitality, celebration, and plain good humor come easily, and social luck runs a little above baseline. Meetings go smoothly, kindness appears where you did not expect it, and small fortunate timings, the right person in the right room, cluster around the pass. The tradition is nearly unanimous about the flavor and equally consistent about the caveat: everything enjoyable is available in slightly too large a portion. Appetite grows with the goodwill. Spending swells to match the mood, sweets and comforts multiply, promises get made banquet-sized, and the golden glow can varnish a plan or a person who deserves a plainer look. None of it is dangerous; all of it invoices later. Venus does not stay long at this table. As she approaches, optimism rises first, a loosened, sociable feeling that the week is going to be good. The exact pass is the season's high table, the best day or two for the party, the proposal, the generous gesture, the ask you have been saving for a warm moment. Separating, the shine settles gently, leaving the goodwill you banked and the receipts you signed. The pass recurs roughly yearly and lasts days, sometimes toward two weeks; in some years Venus's occasional retrograde brings it back for an encore or two, an unusually kind stretch with a reflective middle. Used deliberately, this transit is for planting goodwill where you want it to grow. Reconciliations attempted now start warmer. Requests for help meet enlarged sympathy. Gratitude expressed under this sky lands with double weight, and celebrations scheduled into it seem to run on rails. The growth on offer is a quiet correction many people need: practice at receiving. Pleasure and favor will arrive these few days with little effort from you, and letting them in gracefully, without suspicion and without grabbing, is its own small skill. Take the sweetness at nearly face value, keep one eye on the tab, and the pass leaves both your relationships and your morale a size larger.

Small good fortune knocks quietly when Venus reaches a sextile to your natal Jupiter. The two friendliest planets in the traditional sky link at an angle that offers rather than delivers, and for a few days the social and material world tilts mildly in your favor: an invitation with promise in it, a kindness from someone with reach, a discount, an introduction, a door left agreeably ajar. Nothing spectacular belongs to this transit, and expecting fireworks is the surest way to overlook what it actually brings. Its gifts are connective. Jupiter widens whatever Venus touches, so the pass favors meeting friends of friends, joining something larger than your usual circle, asking a favor of someone senior, or showing generosity that will be remembered out of proportion to its cost. Goodwill compounds unusually well right now; a warm gesture made this week tends to travel. The mood itself is worth something too. Optimism and affection rise together, tolerance widens, and people who normally tire you seem easier to enjoy, which makes the pass a decent window for mending fences at low stakes. The transit keeps its voice down throughout. Applying, you may only register better spirits and a faint sense of social possibility. Around the exact pass the offers concentrate, and acceptance matters more than initiative: say yes to the plausible ones and one often pays off downstream. Separating, the window closes without ceremony, and untouched invitations lapse quietly. Venus brings this angle around roughly twice a year for a few days at a time, and in some years a retrograde repeats a pass, returning an offer you let drift by. Since a sextile only ever proposes, the discipline it asks is simply responsiveness. The people who report luck under this transit are almost always the ones who went to the thing. There is no cost for sitting it out except the invisible kind, the friendship not started, the favor not banked. Over years of small taken chances, these unremarkable few days do real work: they are how a life accumulates warm connections that later look like luck. Answer the knock while it is knocking, and let the modest scale of the transit keep your expectations friendly and your follow-through easy.

Too much of a good thing has its own transit, and this is it. Venus square your natal Jupiter puts the planet of pleasure at a hard angle to the planet of more, and for a few days your sense of enough goes unreliable. The mood is genuinely warm; squares between benefics do not bring hardship so much as excess with friction in it. You want to indulge, treat, celebrate, and promise, all at a scale the moment does not quite support, and the square forces the mismatch into view. Common forms are familiar: the cart filled past the budget, the second dessert and the third, a grand social commitment made in a glow and regretted once the calendar fills, flattery given or received a size too large, sentimentality standing in for actual feeling. In relationships the aspect can inflate gestures past their sincerity, yours or someone else's, and part of the pass's work is noticing when warmth is being performed at volume rather than meant. Money and comfort are the usual arenas, but the deeper subject is judgment about pleasure: what you actually value versus what merely glitters at you while your optimism is loud. Applying, appetite and generosity swell together and everything enjoyable starts to look affordable. Near the exact pass the overreach tends to land somewhere concrete, a purchase, a promise, an indulgence with a next-day tax, or simply the flat feeling that follows a pleasure taken past its peak. Separating, proportion returns fast, and with it a clear, faintly rueful view of the week's receipts. The angle recurs roughly twice a year and runs days, not weeks; in some years a Venus retrograde revisits it once or twice, and a lesson about excess gets a review session. Waiting works better here than refusing. The square punishes nothing except autopilot, and most of its overreaches dissolve if given one night's sleep before signing. Keep the warmth, keep even some of the extravagance, chosen on purpose, and let the pass do what hard aspects between kind planets do best: mark the line where your genuine pleasures end and your habits of more begin. People who learn that line under small pressure like this rarely have to learn it later under large.

Ease with a wide margin is the signature of Venus trine your natal Jupiter. The two benefics link at the smoothest angle they can make, and for up to a week the general climate of your life turns mild and faintly fortunate. Nothing insists, nothing confronts; things simply go a little better than the odds said they would. Social warmth is the most visible layer. People are glad to see you, gatherings run on their own goodwill, differences that usually need managing manage themselves, and your company is easy because you are at ease. Underneath runs a broader favor: matters of money, taste, and affection move without the usual friction, and modest good news has a way of arriving during the pass, the kind that improves a week rather than a year. The tradition rates this among the most agreeable transits and pairs the rating with its standard footnote: agreeable is not the same as productive. A trine supplies flow and charges nothing for it, so the whole pass can be spent in contented drift, and about twice a year it will offer itself again regardless, which makes squandering one feel costless. It nearly is. Still, a little aim multiplies the return. Goodwill this abundant is capital, and the days suit anything that runs on favor: launching a request, hosting, introducing people who should know each other, resolving a standing awkwardness while everyone's patience is wide, enjoying your people in a way they can feel. Contentment rises without obvious cause as Venus closes the angle. Her stay at exact is the broad warm middle, generosity flowing both directions, timing gently on your side, and afterward the climate cools by such small degrees that the transit usually ends unnoticed. In some years a retrograde stretches the visit into repeat passes over a longer season of unusual pleasantness. There is a quiet inner use for all this comfort as well. Weeks like these show you your life with the anxiety turned down, and what you find yourself enjoying when nothing needs defending is reliable information about what you value. Note it. The trine asks nothing, offers plenty, and rewards even light participation; take the warmth seriously enough to spend some of it on purpose, and its afterglow stays useful long past the pass.

Generosity comes at you from across the table when Venus opposes your natal Jupiter. This is a confrontation in the friendliest costume a transit can wear: what faces you is not an enemy but an abundance, someone else's largeness of gesture, appetite, or promise, asking how much you will take on. Invitations arrive oversized. A partner or friend proposes more than the plan needs, a host insists, a deal glitters, a warm person overpromises in perfect sincerity. You stand at the receiving end, deciding where enough sits. Your own responses inflate to match. Oppositions run on shared enthusiasm, and between the two benefics the enthusiasm is real, just unmeasured. The days rarely feel hard. The classic risks are soft ones, indulgence trading as connection, agreement given to keep a glow alive, social or financial commitments accepted at banquet scale and paid for at kitchen scale later. There can also be a subtler imbalance: too much taking or too much giving, one side of a relationship playing benefactor until the ledger quietly tilts. The opposition makes such tilts visible, which is its actual gift. Applying, the sense of social plenty builds. Calendars fill, offers warm up, and other people's mood of more starts to feel like your own. The exact pass usually delivers the centerpiece: the event, the proposal, the lavish gesture, the bargain where both sides are charmed and neither is precise. Separating, sober arithmetic returns, and within days the real value of what was offered sorts itself from the sparkle. Venus keeps the meeting short, days usually, sometimes closer to two weeks, and does not stage it again for about a year. In some years a Venus retrograde brings second and third contacts, and a generous arrangement gets talked back down to its true size across the repeats. The skill the transit exercises is gracious limits. Declining a third helping without insulting the cook, accepting real generosity without keeping score, matching a big gesture with an honest one instead of a bigger one, these are small social arts, and this sky is their practice room. Done even moderately well, the period leaves warmth without residue: relationships enlarged by what was genuinely shared, unburdened by what was merely performed. You come away knowing better what plenty you can hold, and that measure serves every abundant season after.
